story_position: Chapter 3 — Beat 10 — The Recent Reader / Hall of Seals
scene_purpose: Follow the recent reader's physical citation trail from the Beat-9 open table into the Hall of Seals; materially advance the royal-seal investigation through historical evidence that working royal seals could retain magical authority in the physical object; establish older pre-Yahtrean Diysean authority-seal precedent and a Westways scholarly connection; confirm that the recent reader reached the same restricted material first; and end at the threshold of older protected command chambers without identifying the reader, the seal culprit, the exact imbuing method, or any later Card revelation.

sections: Beat 10 — The Recent Reader / Hall of Seals

scene_context_seed.location_name: Old City buried collections leading into the Hall of Seals and older restricted chambers
scene_context_seed.runtime_note: Begin at the still-open Beat-9 research table. Let the characters follow the citation trail naturally instead of verbally reconstructing a checklist. The Hall of Seals is a physical royal antiquarian archive built into older Diysean structure: signets, matrices, impressions, keeper ledgers, regalia records, old fragments, wards, cases, and carved authority marks. No digital/interface language.

hard_outcomes: The party follows the recent reader's citation trail into the Hall of Seals.

The Hall establishes that older working Yahtrean royal seals could retain recognizable magical authority in the physical seal object between uses; this does not require the ruler to consciously cast fresh magic into every document at the moment of sealing.
Older keeper records refer to specialized renewal or maintenance of working seals, but the exact imbuing or renewal method remains missing or incomplete.

Older Diysean physical seals or authority marks provide strong evidence that comparable magical civic or command seal practices predate Yahtrea without proving direct unbroken lineage to Lysara's current seal.

Historical Hall material connects the Diysean ruins in the Westways to prior authority-seal scholarship or recovered authority-mark fragments without proving the Card and seal share one magical origin.
Physical evidence in the Hall confirms the recent reader reached these same materials before the party and deliberately followed the oldest references farther inward.
The party follows that trail toward older protected command chambers and reaches their threshold.
The First Command Warden confrontation does not begin until Beat 11.
production_cost_ceiling: playable Hall exploration with two or three short authored stops and a threshold handoff into Beat 11
